title: My favorite ab isolation exercises
summary: He shows two quick, stretch-focused ab isolation finishers done at the end of a workout: a straight-leg crunch alternating band-assisted and bodyweight reps (upper abs/obliques), and a dumbbell-between-the-feet lying leg raise alternating loaded and bodyweight reps (lower abs). Abs should take 5-6 minutes, done non-stop as supersets, on top of daily hanging leg raise supersets.

claims.claim: Compound movements train the abs to an extent, but as with any muscle, maximizing size and look requires direct isolation.
He likes to train abs every day but doesn't want to spend much time on them; his default is to superset everything with hanging leg raises or hanging knee raises.
Ab work should take five or six minutes at most; he used to spend 30 minutes on abs and no longer needs to.
For abs, the stretch matters more than the contraction because you already get the contraction from bracing during squats and deadlifts; that is why leg raises are so good.
Do crunches with the legs straight: with knees up people tend to use too much lower back, do jerky motions, and miss the stretch.
Two finisher structures: start with band assistance then move to the harder unassisted version, or start loaded to tire the abs fast and then finish with bodyweight.
On crunches keep the head and back long rather than curled; rounding reinforces bad posture, while staying straight puts more load on the core.
What matters on these ab movements is the slow negative; the positive can be explosive and using the arms to come back up is fine.
Alternate unassisted and band-assisted reps non-stop with no rest; doing that for five minutes is plenty of ab work.
The straight-leg crunch hits mostly upper abs and sides, while the dumbbell lying leg raise targets the lower abs.
End-of-workout abs should be done non-stop as supersets so you finish fast; alternating dumbbell and bodyweight leg raises you won't last 10 minutes.
He does only basic ab work but wants his lower abs to show; as his bodyfat comes down over a long period these isolation moves support that goal.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise / hanging knee raise
exercises.why: daily ab base work emphasizing the stretch

exercises.name: Band-assisted straight-leg crunch
cues: band anchored to rack, further away = more assistance
legs straight, arms in front, finish arms overhead
stretch head back, don't curl up or round the back
oblique variation: twist to one side
exercises.why: assistance lets you keep doing slow negatives once pre-fatigued; targets upper abs and obliques

exercises.name: Bodyweight straight-leg crunch
cues: using arms to come up is fine
when you can't hold the negative, stretch fully and roll back up
go back to the band when you fail, then back to bodyweight
exercises.why: harder variation after band pre-fatigue; focus on the negative

exercises.name: Dumbbell lying leg raise (dumbbell between feet)
cues: any weight, even 2 lb; he uses 10 lb
don't raise all the way up or the dumbbell falls
don't bounce feet off the floor; cut ROM if needed
switch to bodyweight leg raises when you fail with the load

exercises.name: Side-lying leg raise
cues: lie on your side and raise the leg
exercises.why: little stretch but a flexing/stabilizing component for the obliques
